hint.element.assembled.fill: What fills the front frame: panel, glass or nothing. A display front leaves the opening empty, so the cabinet interior shows through.
hint.element.bathMixer.bodyDiameter: Mixer body diameter. Sets the part's scale next to the spout and lever; it doesn't affect connections.
hint.element.bathMixer.bodyLength: Mixer body length from wall flange to lever. A longer body protrudes further over the bath rim.
hint.element.bathMixer.centres: Distance between inlet centers; 150 mm is standard in Russia. If it doesn't match the wall outlets, the mixer won't fit them.
hint.element.bathMixer.escutcheonReach: How far the cover flange projects from the wall. It hides the supply outlets; a short projection leaves them exposed.
hint.element.bathMixer.outletDiameter: Diameter of the connector for the hose or spout. It must match the fitting's connection size.
hint.element.bathMixer.spout: Spout length from body to tip. A short spout pours onto the bath rim; a long one gets in the way when stepping into the shower.
hint.element.bathtub.bowlDepth: Bowl depth from rim to bottom. It sets how much water the tub holds and can't exceed the bathtub height.
hint.element.bathtub.bowlFillet: Rounding where the bowl bottom meets its walls. More rounding is comfier to sit in but leaves less usable volume at the bottom.
hint.element.bathtub.bowlRadius: Corner radius of the bowl in plan. A larger radius gives a softer outline; a smaller one is closer to rectangular.
hint.element.bathtub.rimWidth: Rim width around the perimeter. The rim holds the mixer and supports the bath panel, but every extra millimeter comes out of the bowl.
hint.element.bed.headboard: Adds a headboard. It increases the bed's overall height, not its length or width.
hint.element.bed.size: Single and double beds differ in width: 900 mm vs 1800 mm, both 2000 mm long. Changing the type overwrites the bed's dimensions.
hint.element.cooktop.cutout: Opening the hob cuts in the worktop. It is never larger than the hob; for a known model it comes from the spec sheet and is locked.
hint.element.door.sash: A glazed door leaf lets light in from the next room; a solid one lets none through.
hint.element.drawer.boxWidth: Width of the box itself, not the front. The inner size for the runners is recalculated automatically, so don't subtract clearances.
hint.element.drawer.color: Color of the drawer sides and bottom. It doesn't affect runners or front; interior finish only.
hint.element.drawer.length: Runner length. It must fit the cabinet depth, or the drawer hits the back panel and won't close fully.
hint.element.drawer.type: Side height decides what fits in the drawer and what opening it takes: from 86 mm for cutlery to 200 mm for pots.
hint.element.drawer.upperLength: Runner length of the upper drawer in a pair. Set independently of the lower one; their systems aren't linked.
hint.element.duct.airflow: Design airflow through this duct section, used for the air velocity check (VNT-01).
hint.element.duct.height: Height of the rectangular duct section.
hint.element.duct.profile: Duct cross-section: round pipe or rectangular. Determines which size fields below apply.
hint.element.duct.width: Width of the rectangular duct section.
hint.element.facade.doorMode: Hinge side and opening direction of the front. It decides whether the open door clashes with its neighbor or a handle.
hint.element.fence.pitDepth: Post hole depth from ground level. In frost-heaving soils, holes go deeper, below the frost depth.
hint.element.fence.postSection: Steel tube section of the post. Affects the hole diameter and the concrete volume per post in the bill of materials.
hint.element.fence.postStep: Post spacing along the fence; it sets how many posts the fence length needs.
hint.element.fence.sheetMark: Profiled sheet grade. It sets the effective sheet width and thus the number of sheets for the fence length.
hint.element.floorSlab.concrete: Concrete class of this slab only. It affects this slab's line in the bill of materials, not the whole project.
hint.element.floorSlab.rebarDiameter: Bar diameter of the slab's reinforcement mesh. Used to calculate rebar weight in the bill of materials.
hint.element.floorSlab.rebarStep: Mesh spacing in both directions. Smaller spacing means more bars and more rebar weight.
hint.element.floorSlab.technology: A cast-in-place slab calculates its own concrete and rebar. Beam floors have no calculation yet, so their concrete and rebar fields are hidden.
hint.element.foundation.compacted: Bedding compaction. Without it, minimum sand and gravel thickness isn't checked: loose bedding behaves differently and 100 mm guarantees nothing.
hint.element.foundation.concrete: Concrete class of this footing only. It is listed next to the volume in the bill of materials, so footings of different classes aren't summed together.
hint.element.foundation.cover: Concrete cover over the rebar. With less than two bar diameters, the rebar risks exposure and rust.
hint.element.foundation.frostDepth: Depth below which the ground doesn't freeze; the footing is laid below it. Calculated from the project region and this footing's soil; not editable here.
hint.element.foundation.gravel: Crushed stone bedding thickness under the footing, on top of the sand. Same 100 mm limit as the sand.
hint.element.foundation.rebarDiameter: Diameter of the longitudinal bars and stirrups. Together with the cover, it decides whether the rebar could end up exposed.
hint.element.foundation.rebarStep: Stirrup spacing along the footing. If it exceeds the footing width, the cage no longer holds its shape.
hint.element.foundation.sand: Sand bedding thickness under the footing. Below 100 mm with compaction on, it no longer works as a levelling and drainage layer.
hint.element.foundation.soil: Soil under this strip footing; it overrides the project setting. It sets the minimum footing width and the frost depth below.
hint.element.grille.airflow: Design airflow through the grille, used for the room air exchange check (VNT-03).
hint.element.laundry.kind: Washer and dryer are the same unit under two names: only the scene label and the specification line change. Size and door stay the same.
hint.element.light.beamAngle: Width of the light cone. A narrow angle gives an accent spot; a wide one floods the whole work area evenly.
hint.element.light.diffusion: How far the light reaches: the slider moves the radius between 'Radius at 0%' and 'Radius at 100%'. Left is a spot under the lamp, right is the whole room.
hint.element.light.drop: How far the light source sits below the lamp body. Without it, the body blocks the beam and casts a ring of shadow below.
hint.element.light.efficacy: Lumens per watt: about 110 for LED, a quarter of that for incandescent. Together with power, this is the lamp's brightness.
hint.element.light.glow: Brightness of the shade itself in the shot, as if lit from within. Affects only how the lamp looks, not room lighting.
hint.element.light.lumensPerUnit: Lumens per unit of scene brightness. A global calibration: adjust it when all lights at once look too bright or too dim.
hint.element.light.power: Power times efficacy gives the light output: 9 W at 110 lm/W is about 1000 lumens. Higher power brightens the whole scene, not just the lamp.
hint.element.light.range: Beam range at the left end of the diffusion slider, in millimeters. With 'Radius at 100%' it sets the slider's full span.
hint.element.light.rangeMax: Beam range at the right end of the diffusion slider, in millimeters. With 'Radius at 0%' it sets the slider's full span.
hint.element.light.shadow: The lamp can cast no shadow, a hard one, or a soft one with a blurred edge. Soft costs more to render but looks real.
hint.element.light.shadowStrength: Shadow opacity. At 100 it is a black void with no detail; at 0 the shadow disappears.
hint.element.light.shape: A shade shines in a cone down with some light up; a globe shines equally in all directions. Up cone and up light don't apply to a globe.
hint.element.light.softness: Transition from the bright center of the spot to darkness. At 0 the edge is a sharp circle; at 100 it blurs out completely.
hint.element.light.temperature: Light color: 2700 K is warm evening yellow, 4000 K neutral working light, 6000 K cool daylight. It sets the mood of the whole shot.
hint.element.light.upCone: Up cone width as a fraction of the main beam. Narrow draws a crisp spot on the ceiling; wide gives an even wash.
hint.element.light.upLight: Share of light sent up to the ceiling. The reflected glow keeps the room from looking lit by a single spotlight.
hint.element.light.upRange: Up cone range as a fraction of the main beam's range. Works with 'Up light'; without it, this has no visible effect.
hint.element.pillar.diameter: Column diameter along its full height. Capital and base use the same diameter as the middle section.
hint.element.pillar.midHeight: Straight section between the 20 mm capital and 10 mm base; it sets the total height. Allowed from 50 to 100 mm, other values are clamped.
hint.element.pipe.derived: Outer and inner diameter and wall thickness come from the nominal bore and can't be edited here.
hint.element.pipe.nominalBore: Nominal bore is a pipe size designation, not the outer diameter. Outer and inner diameter and wall thickness are filled in automatically.
hint.element.pipeFitting.bore: Port diameter comes from the connected pipe and can't be edited. To change it, change the pipe size.
hint.element.pouffe.seatThickness: Thickness of the upholstered top. The rest of the height goes to the base, so a thick cushion leaves short legs.
hint.element.radial.cornerRadius: Outer corner radius of the curved shelf. A larger radius rounds the corner more but leaves less usable depth there.
hint.element.roof.overhangMm: Roof overhang beyond the wall face. Enlarges the roof outline equally on all sides.
hint.element.roof.pitchDeg: Slope angle from horizontal. Affects ridge height and roofing area in the bill of materials.
hint.element.roof.rafterStepMm: Rafter spacing along the eaves; it sets the number of rafters in the bill of materials.
hint.element.roof.ridgeAxis: Axis the ridge runs along. 'Auto' picks the longer side of the top-story wall outline.
hint.element.roof.type: Roof type: mono-pitch, gable or hip. The shape and number of slopes change with the type.
hint.element.screwLeg.baseDiameter: Diameter of the fixed foot. Larger is more stable but more visible below the plinth.
hint.element.screwLeg.baseHeight: Height of the fixed foot the leg stands on. It adds to the thread length for total height, so changing it also moves the host part.
hint.element.screwLeg.thread: The thread must match the threaded insert in the part the leg supports, or there is nothing to screw it into.
hint.element.screwLeg.threadLength: The thread extends the leg to the floor: unscrewing it raises the part. Total leg height changes with this field.
hint.element.seat.seatHeight: Seat height from the floor. The backrest fills the rest of the overall height, so raising the seat shortens the backrest.
hint.element.shape.cornerRadius: Corner radius in plan. Zero gives a square corner; half the shorter side makes the part round, which is the maximum allowed.
hint.element.showerColumn.armReach: Reach of the overhead shower from the riser. The longer it is, the closer the spray is to the tray center and the further from the wall you stand.
hint.element.showerColumn.columnHeight: Total height from floor to overhead shower. A column taller than the room will hit the ceiling.
hint.element.showerColumn.handDiameter: Hand shower diameter. Affects only how it looks, not water pressure.
hint.element.showerColumn.headDiameter: Overhead shower diameter. A larger head gives a wider rain spray overhead.
hint.element.showerColumn.headThickness: Overhead shower thickness. A thin head looks lighter but is less rigid at the end of the arm.
hint.element.showerColumn.hoseLength: Hand shower hose length. A short hose won't reach the far edge of the shower tray.
hint.element.showerColumn.riserDiameter: Diameter of the vertical riser. Sets the visible pipe thickness; it doesn't affect water supply.
hint.element.showerColumn.wallOffset: How far the riser stands off the wall. The gap keeps the hose and holder off the tiles, but it also takes space in the shower.
hint.element.table.legInset: How far the legs are set in from the edge of the top. More inset gives more knee room at the ends but less stability.
hint.element.toilet.flushPlate: Height of the flush button in the wall. Align it with the tile rows so the plate doesn't land on a joint.
hint.element.toilet.seatHeight: Height from floor to seat. It sets the sitting height; for a wall-hung toilet it is set by the in-wall frame, not the bowl.
hint.element.wall.joint: Mortar joint of this wall, in mm. Thicker joints mean fewer blocks and more mortar for the same wall.
hint.element.wall.loadBearing: A load-bearing wall carries the floor slab: it can't be removed and openings in it are limited. Unchecked, the wall is a partition.
hint.element.wall.masonry: Material of this wall; it overrides the project setting. It decides how the wall is counted in the bill of materials: units, cubic meters or studs.
hint.element.wall.waste: Breakage and cutting allowance for this wall, in percent. Added to the unit count; it doesn't affect mortar.
hint.element.wallDevice.plateHeight: Height of the socket or switch frame. Sets the size of the wall cutout for the back box.
hint.element.wallDevice.plateWidth: Width of the socket or switch frame. It must match the number of gangs: a narrow frame won't fit all modules.
hint.element.wallDevice.posts: Number of gangs in one frame. A two- or three-gang block takes as much width as its gangs combined.
hint.element.wallDevice.powered: The switch turns its group's lamps on and off right in the scene. This is the light state in the image, not a property of the frame.
hint.element.wallDevice.protrusion: How far the frame stands out from the wall. It decides whether a cabinet fits flush and whether a front hits the frame.
hint.element.wallLayer.battenStep: Spacing of vertical battens in the ventilated gap; it sets the number and total length of battens in the bill of materials.
hint.element.wallLayer.thickness: Thickness of the insulation, ventilated gap or cladding layer. The layer sits against the wall and follows its length and height, so only thickness needs editing.
hint.element.window.openingMode: Hinge side, and so where the open sash swings. In a narrow passage, a sash on the wrong side blocks the way.
hint.element.window.sill: How far the sill projects into the room. It can stop a tall cabinet from going against the window, so check it against front depth.
hint.element.window.tint: Clear or tinted window glass. Tint reduces daylight in the room and hides the interior from outside.
hint.settings.construction.compacted: Marks the bedding as compacted. Without compaction the layer settles and the footing loses support.
hint.settings.construction.concrete: Compressive strength class of the strip footing concrete. Used in the bill of materials and the reinforcement check.
hint.settings.construction.floorHeight: Clear story height, floor to ceiling. New walls get this height, and masonry volume is calculated from it.
hint.settings.construction.frostDepth: Depth below which the ground doesn't freeze; the strip footing goes below it. Derived from region and soil per SP 22.13330; the lines below name the station, or the reason when there is no value.
hint.settings.construction.gravel: Thickness of crushed stone over the sand. It spreads the load and stops capillary water reaching the footing.
hint.settings.construction.joint: Mortar joint thickness between blocks. Thicker joints mean fewer blocks per wall and more mortar.
hint.settings.construction.masonry: Material for new walls. Its format decides how a wall is counted: by units, cubic meters or frame studs.
hint.settings.construction.neighbourLeve: How stories other than the open one are drawn: in full (as in The Sims 2), dimmed or hidden. Storeys above the current one are always hidden.
hint.settings.construction.region: The region sets the site climate, which determines the frost depth for the foundation. Change it if the site is outside your usual area.
hint.settings.construction.sand: Thickness of the sand layer under the footing. It levels the base and drains water away from the concrete.
hint.settings.construction.slabThickness: Default thickness of cast-in-place slabs for new 'Floor slab' elements. Each slab can override it in its own properties.
hint.settings.construction.soil: Site soil sets the minimum footing width and embedment requirements. 'Unknown' is treated as the worst case, to stay safe.
hint.settings.construction.waste: Allowance for breakage, cutting and losses when laying. The calculated unit count is increased by this percentage.
hint.settings.control.arrowSpeed: Camera movement speed with the arrow keys. Works like WASD, handy when the mouse is busy selecting or dragging.
hint.settings.control.mouseInvertX: The camera turns left when the mouse moves right. For those who prefer to pull the scene along rather than push it.
hint.settings.control.mouseInvertY: The camera tilts down when the mouse moves up. For those who feel the mouse moves the camera itself, not the view from it.
hint.settings.control.mouseSensitivity: How fast the camera turns when you drag with the mouse. Lower it if the view jerks; raise it if turning is too slow.
hint.settings.control.perfRecordingFile: While performance measurement runs, data is written to test-results/perf/perf_<date> (CSV). Click again to stop recording; measurement stays on.
hint.settings.control.wasdSpeed: Camera movement speed with the WASD keys. Raise it to cross large kitchens quickly; lower it to fine-tune the angle.
hint.settings.light.ambient: Overall level of shadowless fill light. Raise it if dark recesses and cabinet bottoms can't be made out.
hint.settings.light.bloomClamp: Upper limit of glow strength. Keeps very bright sources from swelling into a solid white patch.
hint.settings.light.bloomStrength: Glow strength of bright areas such as lamps and gloss highlights. Higher values make halos around lights more visible.
hint.settings.light.bloomThreshold: Brightness at which an area starts to glow. A lower threshold makes medium-bright surfaces glow too, not just lamps.
hint.settings.light.bounceMax: Maximum number of light bounces in the lighting calculation. More bounces light far corners more evenly but take longer.
hint.settings.light.contrast: Difference between dark and light areas of the frame. Higher contrast gives deeper shadows and brighter highlights.
hint.settings.light.equator: Diffuse light arriving horizontally from the sides. Increase it if the sides of furniture look flat and lack volume.
hint.settings.light.exposure: Overall frame brightness in exposure stops. Plus brightens the whole scene, minus darkens it, like a camera's shutter speed.
hint.settings.light.floorBounce: Share of light bounced off the floor back onto walls and furniture. Increase it if lower surfaces look gloomier than they should.
hint.settings.light.lampShadows: Scene lamps cast their own shadows. Turn off if lamp shadows make small nearby details hard to read.
hint.settings.light.saturation: Color saturation of the frame. At zero the image turns black and white; above 100% colors look garish.
hint.settings.light.shadowDistance: Distance from the camera up to which sun shadows are drawn. Further shows shadows deeper in the shot but costs more to compute.
hint.settings.light.sky: Intensity of light from above, like a ceiling light or roof window. Increase it if cabinet tops look dark.
hint.settings.light.sunShadowStrength: How dark the sun's shadow is. At zero it disappears; at maximum it is a black void with no detail.
hint.settings.light.tonemap: Maps HDR brightness to the screen range. 'Neutral' keeps colors as they are; 'ACES' adds contrast but shifts hues in highlights.
hint.settings.light.vignetteStrength: How much the frame edges darken. At zero there is no vignette; at maximum the corners are almost black.
hint.settings.photo.ambientOcclusion: Darkens corners, gaps and junctions, adding depth to the kitchen. Furniture stops looking pasted onto the walls and floor.
hint.settings.photo.antiAliasing: Removes jagged edges on thin lines and diagonals. Without it, cabinet and appliance outlines look stepped.
hint.settings.photo.aoDirect: Share of ambient occlusion darkening applied to directly lit areas. Lower it if dark blotches appear on brightly lit surfaces.
hint.settings.photo.aoFalloff: Distance in meters over which ambient occlusion fades out. Increase it if AO doesn't reach deep recesses, shelves and inside corners.
hint.settings.photo.aoFullRes: Computes ambient occlusion at full resolution instead of half. Shadows in corners and joints get sharper, but the pass takes longer.
hint.settings.photo.aoIntensity: How much occluded areas darken. At 0% the effect is invisible; at high values corners turn almost black.
hint.settings.photo.aoRadius: Distance in millimeters within which AO looks for occluded areas. A small radius brings out fine gaps; a large one darkens corners overall.
hint.settings.photo.bloom: Bright areas spread into a soft halo, as in a camera. Lamps and highlights on fronts get a natural glow.
hint.settings.photo.ceiling: The ceiling follows the height of visible walls. When walls are lowered to the worktop, the ceiling drops too, so the room doesn't look like an empty box.
hint.settings.photo.hdr: Keeps detail in the brightest and darkest areas. Without HDR, highlights blow out to white and shadows lose texture.
hint.settings.photo.lightsPerObject: How many nearest lights count toward an object's shadows. More lights give softer penumbras, but each frame takes longer to render.
hint.settings.photo.renderScale: Renders at this percentage of the window resolution: lower is faster but blurrier, 100% is full sharpness.
hint.settings.photo.shadowMap: Size of the texture shadows are drawn on. More pixels give sharper shadow edges but more load on the graphics card.
hint.settings.photo.shadows: Shadows from the sun and lamps. Turn off for fast flat lighting while you tune other settings.
hint.settings.photo.softShadows: Smooths shadow edges into a soft blend instead of a hard line. Rendering slows down, but shadows look natural.
hint.settings.photo.ssgi: Computes indirect light: light bouncing off one surface reaches its neighbors. The shot looks more realistic, but render time rises noticeably.
hint.settings.photo.ssgiBlur: Blur applied to the SSGI result, in pixels. It removes grain, but too much blurs lighting detail.
hint.settings.photo.ssgiRadius: Distance in millimeters within which SSGI looks for reflections. Larger lets light spread further but slows rendering.
hint.settings.photo.ssgiResolution: Resolution SSGI is computed at. 100% is full but slow; lowering it speeds up rendering at the cost of grain.
hint.settings.photo.ssgiSamples: Number of samples for bounced light. More samples mean less noise, but each frame takes longer.
hint.settings.photo.ssgiStrength: How strongly bounced light affects the scene. At 0% there is no effect; at 100% nearby surfaces pass on the most color.
hint.settings.photo.supersampling: Renders the frame at double resolution, then scales it down. Fine detail gets sharper, but frame time rises noticeably.
hint.settings.photo.vignette: Slightly darkens the frame edges to draw the eye to the center, mimicking lens vignetting.
hint.settings.project.autoSave: Saves the project in the background at regular intervals. The interval is a separate field below.
hint.settings.project.autoSaveInterval: Seconds between autosaves. A shorter interval means less risk of losing edits in a crash.
hint.settings.project.blockOnViolation: Blocks edits that break placement rules. Turn off to keep the violation on screen and fix it later.
hint.settings.project.cameraPanFree: Camera panning is not limited to the kitchen area. Handy when working on a large house or site.
hint.settings.project.edgePartialThresho: Minimum share of an edge, in percent, that must be exposed for edge banding to be applied. Raise it if banding appears on short edges against a wall.
hint.settings.project.grid: A floor grid helps align parts by eye. Grid spacing is set in a separate field below.
hint.settings.project.gridStep: Distance between floor grid lines. Finer spacing is a more precise guide but makes the grid denser on screen.
hint.settings.project.snap: Snapping pulls a dragged part to neighbors and walls. The snap distance is a separate field below.
hint.settings.project.snapThreshold: Distance at which a part snaps to its neighbors. A larger threshold makes snapping kick in sooner.
hint.settings.project.spatialGrid: Speeds up overlap checks between objects. Unnoticeable on small projects, but a clear speed-up on large kitchens with dozens of cabinets.
hint.settings.view.hideLightSources: Hides the lamp and fixture models while their light keeps working. Useful for a clean shot.
hint.settings.view.hideOpeningsOnLowered: Windows and doors are hidden along with the lowered part of the wall. Otherwise they float in the air above the cut.
hint.settings.view.lowerAllWalls: Lowers every wall at once, not just those nearest the camera. Useful for a top-down view of the whole room.
hint.settings.view.lowerNearWalls: Walls between the camera and the kitchen are cut down to worktop height. The view opens up while the room layout stays visible.
hint.settings.view.objectOutline: Draws a thin line around each object, separating neighboring cabinets with the same decor.
hint.settings.view.objects: Hide furniture and appliances, leaving only walls and openings. Handy when editing the room itself.
hint.settings.view.preset: Each mode keeps its own set of display settings. This switch picks which mode's set you are editing.
hint.settings.view.wallOutline: Draws a thin line along wall edges, so adjacent walls of the same color don't merge into one patch.
hint.settings.view.walls: Hide all walls to arrange furniture from above without looking through them.

input.captureKey: Click, then press a key. Esc cancels.

settings.control.ref.catalogFocus: While another input field has focus, the catalog ignores Enter, arrows, [ / ] and Escape — the tile selection stays but does nothing
settings.control.ref.catalogKeys: Parts catalog: in the search field ↓ moves to the tile grid; in the grid ← → ↑ ↓ — neighboring tile, Enter places the selected one, [ / ] changes the variant, Escape clears the tile selection
settings.control.ref.ctrlSnap: Ctrl + drag or resize — invert snapping (on/off)
settings.control.ref.escapeOrder: Escape closes one thing per press, in this order: drag → light link picker → measurement → eyedropper → delete confirmation → context menu → group menu → catalog tile → catalog → day/night panel → music
settings.control.ref.panLmb: Panning also starts with LMB on empty space, not only with its own gesture
settings.mcp.aboutText: The program gives an AI agent access to the open project over the MCP protocol. The agent places cabinets, aligns fronts, finds collisions and builds the specification right in your scene — changes show up immediately and undo works as usual.
settings.mcp.agentPrompt:
Connect me to Kitchen Designer via MCP.

The server is already running on this computer and waiting for a connection:
  {0}
Transport — Streamable HTTP, no authorization, listens on localhost only.

Add it to your configuration under the name {1}. For example:
  Claude Code:      claude mcp add --transport http {2} {3}
  Cursor / VS Code: an entry with "url": "{4}"
  Codex:            [mcp_servers.{5}]  url = "{6}"

Once connected, call the ping tool and tell me what it answered, then read get_project_instructions. If the server is unavailable, the Kitchen Designer program is closed — ask me to open it.
settings.mcp.connectHint: The button copies a short text with the server address to the clipboard. Paste it to the agent and it will connect by itself.
settings.mcp.guideLocal: is next to the program, no internet needed
settings.mcp.guideMissing: The guide was not found next to the program. It is also available here:
settings.mcp.statusHint: The bridge starts together with the program. While it is open, the agent has something to connect to.
